subject: Contract route & payment routing — confirmation of procurement path and billing start
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jerry Holt <jerry.holt@aerosense.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract route & payment routing — confirmation of procurement path and billing start

Hi Jerry — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has everything they need: 

1) Procurement route: AeroSense prefers a PO-based cycle (standard net-30) for first-year commitments. They also asked about card payment for initial POC credits as a stopgap.
2) Marketplace: AeroSense is evaluating whether to buy via the Cloud Marketplace (AWS Partner) to simplify billing across teams — you mentioned procurement wanted to know if Redwood appears on marketplace invoices and if costs can be consolidated.
3) Trial conversion criteria: We agreed on two success signals to flip to paid — (a) sustained 50k tokens/day over 5 business days, (b) average 95% of inference responses meeting the latency target (under 250ms p50) for the evaluation prompts.

Attachments: SOW draft + pricing worksheet attached.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll send SOW + pricing for internal review and legal redline (attached).
- Sean to confirm marketplace listing implications and whether Redwood can accept a PO that references a marketplace purchase order.
- Jerry to loop in your procurement contact and share the PO template and preferred PO date.

Can we target a billing start of 2027-04-26 if procurement can provide PO by 2027-04-18? That gives our provisioning team a week to set up dedicated quota and billing rules.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference

From: Jerry Holt <jerry.holt@aerosense.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: AeroSense Procurement <procurement@aerosense.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Contract route & payment routing — confirmation of procurement path and billing start

Vanessa — thanks for the summary. Procurement confirms PO for year 1 (net-30) is preferred. A few clarifications: 

- Marketplace: procurement prefers direct invoicing to our AP system; they can accept a PO that references a marketplace purchase only if the invoice is issued to AeroSense directly (we can’t accept third-party merchant invoices). Does Redwood invoice end-customer if the purchase is via AWS Marketplace?
- Trial thresholds: 50k tokens/day is fine; can we also tie the success signal to a single feature set (batch summarization) rather than all endpoints to make measurement simpler?
- Billing start: PO issuance timeline looks tight; our procurement lead is out next week. We can aim to have a signed PO by 2027-04-20 at the earliest. If that’s acceptable, we still want the option to start paid usage as soon as we cross the threshold even if PO formalities finish after.

I’ve included procurement on cc; procurement@aerosense.com will send the PO template + preferred PO issuance window.

—Jerry
Jerry Holt
Head of Product, AeroSense
jerry.holt@aerosense.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract route & payment routing — confirmation of procurement path and billing start

Vanessa / Monica — quick internal note on the procurement vs marketplace gating: 

- Marketplace invoicing: Redwood can list on AWS Marketplace, but standard marketplace flow issues invoices from the marketplace operator (AWS) as the seller-of-record. We do offer a "direct invoice" option for partners where we can bill AeroSense directly, but that requires a Marketplace Reseller Agreement and a short partner provisioning timeline (usually 7–10 business days).
- PO references: we can accept a PO that references a marketplace commitment if procurement provides a PO to Redwood with the AWS order id included and the AP team accepts the invoice format. That’s doable but will require procurement + our finance to confirm fields.
- Interim card flow: For initial credits/PO staging we can accept a company card to cover the POC credits; we’ll apply those credits toward the first invoice if a PO is issued retroactively.
- Billing start flexibility: We’re comfortable starting billing the day the usage threshold is met and retroactively applying a PO (with invoice replacement) provided procurement signs within 30 days. That solves Jerry’s concern about the procurement lead being out.

Actionable items for us:
- I’ll reach out to finance to pre-authorize direct-invoice listing for AeroSense (if procurement wants direct billing).
- Vanessa: ask AeroSense procurement to send the PO template + confirm whether they will include an AWS order id if they go marketplace route.
- Monica: prepare an internal billing runbook for retroactive PO application and the timeline to replace invoices.

I’ll follow up once finance confirms.
—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Commercial Operations
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jerry Holt <jerry.holt@aerosense.com>, AeroSense Procurement <procurement@aerosense.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract route & payment routing — confirmation of procurement path and billing start

Hi Jerry / Procurement team — thanks for the quick clarification and for sharing the PO template (we received it). Confirming Redwood’s proposal so procurement can take it to legal/AP: 

- Primary path: AeroSense will issue a vendor PO directly to Redwood (vendor: Redwood Inference), net-30 for year 1 commitment. Please include the following on the PO: Redwood Inference EIN 82-3947215, PO reference to deal RDW-2027-9876, and the SOW name "Redwood_SOW_AeroSense_v1".
- Marketplace: If procurement prefers to route via AWS Marketplace, please include the AWS order id on the PO and indicate that the invoice should be issued to AeroSense (we will coordinate with finance to accept the marketplace flow). This needs an extra 7–10 business days for merchant setup.
- Interim card/PO gap: If the PO cannot be delivered by 2027-04-18, we will provision capacity and allow starting paid usage on the day you cross the agreed threshold, with retroactive PO insertion up to 30 days.
- Success criteria: We will scope the trial success to the batch summarization endpoint (as requested). Threshold: 50k tokens/day sustained over 5 business days; latency target 250ms p50 for that endpoint.

Next: procurement to send back the completed PO and preferred billing start date. For legal: we’ve attached the SOW and price sheet you can use as the basis for documents; I’ll also share a DocuSign link for signatures once legal confirms the final SOW redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to getting AeroSense into production.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
